title: Endpoint jumps force a nonintegrable harmonic holonomy tail

endpoint_obstruction.hypothesis: A real compactly supported primitive G is W^{2,1} on finitely many intervals, its intervalwise first derivative has bounded variation, and its merged endpoint jumps are J_r at distinct a_r.
endpoint_obstruction.asymptotic: widehat G(t)=-(it)^(-1)T(t)+O(t^(-2)), where T(t)=sum_r J_r exp(i t a_r).
endpoint_obstruction.mean: If any J_r is nonzero then T is a nonzero finite exponential polynomial, M(|T|^2)=sum_r|J_r|^2>0, and M(|T|)>=M(|T|^2)/||T||_infinity>0.
endpoint_obstruction.obstruction: Dyadic-shell averaging gives int_1^infinity|widehat G(t)|dt=infinity for every nonzero merged endpoint-jump vector.
endpoint_obstruction.sharpness: K1613's zero endpoint trace is sharp in this finite piecewise-BV class; first-derivative jumps remain allowed because they enter at order t^(-2).
endpoint_obstruction.scope_guard: The result does not derive the spectral representation, electric-field L1, nonlinear remainders, scattering, a physical domain, or a source-owned flow.
